tests.name: Scale Behavior — Parse Time Scaling
tests.detail:
Parse time scaling:
| Size | YON | JSON | Ratio |
|------|-----|------|-------|
| 500 | 1.89ms | 0.06ms | 29.23x |
| 2000 | 2.47ms | 0.25ms | 9.78x |
| 5000 | 6.64ms | 0.64ms | 10.42x |
| 10000 | 13.38ms | 1.26ms | 10.60x |

Note: YON streaming parser is higher-level (event-based) compared to native C++ parsers. The advantage is not raw speed but streaming availability — YON delivers data incrementally.

tests.name: Scale Behavior — Record Lookup at 75% depth (5000 records)

comparison.delta: YON can stop at record 3750; JSON must parse all 5000

tests.detail: YON scans line-by-line and stops at record 3750: 5.32ms. JSON must parse the entire 5000-record document first: 0.68ms. Streaming early-termination is the structural advantage.

tests.name: Scale Behavior — Document Size Comparison
tests.detail:
Document size comparison:
| Records | YON | JSON | Ratio |
|---------|-----|------|-------|
| 500 | 49.2KB | 46.2KB | 1.06x |
| 2000 | 199.1KB | 187.3KB | 1.06x |
| 5000 | 500.8KB | 471.5KB | 1.06x |
| 10000 | 1003.7KB | 945.1KB | 1.06x |

YON's tag baseline per record is roughly constant. JSON's structural baseline (brackets, commas, key quoting) grows similarly.

tests.name: Scale Behavior — Token Efficiency at Scale
tests.detail: Token savings at scale: 500 records=-6%, 2000 records=-6%, 5000 records=-6%, 10000 records=-6%. YON's compact tag syntax (@NOTE, @MAP) has lower per-record structural baseline than JSON's {"key":"value"} pattern.
